csm_truss.problem_text:
Study 1: linear elasticity — 13-member planar truss with uncertain member moduli (worst-case compliance under a constitutive knowledge set).
Geometry: Planar truss, statically indeterminate to degree two, 13 members of unit cross-sectional area. Two members meet at an unloaded free node. Node coordinates, member lengths, span and height are not given in the text; there is only a figure (Fig. 2a).
Material: Linear elastic bars with uncertain Young's moduli E in R^13. Per-member bounds are [0.8, 1.2]. One loaded member has [0.75, 1.25]. The two uninterrogated members have [0.6, 1.4]. A batch-mean constraint, |(1/13) sum_e E_e - 1| <= 0.03, couples the members. Moduli are dimensionless/normalised (nominal 1). Units are not stated.
Boundary conditions: Pinned at one support and on a roller at the other support.
Loading: A single nodal load at the top-middle node. Its magnitude and direction are not stated.
Discretisation in the paper: Direct-stiffness truss model K(E) = sum_e E_e K_e with 13 bar elements, one per member. For a pin-jointed truss under nodal loads this is exact, so there is no mesh. Vertex enumeration in the visible quotient uses 2904 candidates.
Features: Nodal point load and pin/roller supports on a pin-jointed truss. In the bar (truss) model, member forces are finite, so there is no stress singularity. There are no corners, notches or cracks in a continuum sense..
Question: which of these quantities can serve as trustworthy reference values: Witness-certified endpoint W(P) (Upper endpoint of the response interval of the value function f(E) = -1/2 c(E), i.e. the stiffest coherent material, obtained by the witness loop. It needed 4/8/11 solves to reach relative width 1e-3/1e-5/1e-7.); inf_P f (Lower endpoint of the value function over P, computed by vertex enumeration in the visible quotient (2904 candidates).); Classical worst-case compliance max_P c (max_P c = -2 inf_P f); Active witnesses / visible members (Number of active witnesses in the dual certificate, and the number of visible members n_vis out of 13.); Value change under motion of uninterrogated members (Change in the value function when the two uninterrogated (invisible) members' moduli are varied. Their identification as invisible is reported as 'yes'.); Random-sample containment check (Whether 22 119 admissible random samples all lie inside the certified interval.); Coherence gap, stiff end (f(E_hi) - W(P), where E_hi is not in P); Coherence gap, soft end (c(E_lo) - max_P c, where E_lo is not in P); Box-only set reproduces f(E_hi) (With per-member bounds only (a lattice), W = f(E_hi) exactly, in 2 solves.); Complementary principle, coupled set, hull certificate (sup f^c on the hull of mapped vertices compared with 1/2 max_P c.); Value-criterion gain G_W(e) (Value-criterion gain of measuring each member's modulus.); Interval-criterion gain G_R, best member (Interval-criterion gain for the most heavily loaded member.); Interval-criterion gain G_R, member chosen by parameter width (G_R of the (uninterrogated) member that the parameter-width criterion selects.)?

card.title: Study 4: assembled composite shell, single-edge-notched tension specimen (finite-strain Reissner–Mindlin phase-field fracture), constitutive-set certification

geometry.value: Single-edge-notched tension specimen modelled as a shell, thickness 1 mm, seeded notch of length 14.4 mm, fibre orientation 30° to the loading direction. In-plane specimen width and height are not stated.
geometry.quote: thickness 1 mm, seeded notch of 14.4 mm, fibre orientation 30◦ to the loading direction;

material.value: Transversely isotropic composite: matrix Em = 70 GPa, νm = 0.3; fibre Ef = 200 GPa, νf = 0.25; λmI = µmII = µLT = 1 GPa; Gc = 50 J/m2, Gc,int = 10 J/m2; ℓc = ℓβ = 5 mm; residual stiffness 1e-7. The energy is split into mechanism potentials Ψf(I4), Ψmx(IT, JT) and Ψint(Jft), plus closed-form terms. The three tensile potentials use the analytic reference law, are represented as cubic B-splines (nraw = 226), or are replaced by a learned law.
material.quote: matrix Em = 70 GPa, νm = 0.3, fibre Ef = 200 GPa, νf = 0.25, λmI = µmII = µLT = 1 GPa,

boundary_conditions.value: Displacement control (tension) up to 20 µm. The section does not say which edges are clamped or loaded, or how the grips are constrained.
boundary_conditions.quote: control to 20 µm in eight increments; increments are solved by alternate minimisation with

loading.value: Applied displacement up to 20 µm in eight increments, using alternate minimisation with load-step bisection. Increment 5 reached 11.25 µm of the scheduled 12.5 µm. The certified increments are k=2 (5.00 µm), k=4 (10.00 µm), k=5 (11.25 µm) and k=8 (20.00 µm). Bending is not exercised.
loading.quote: load-step bisection, the fifth reaching 11.25 µm of the scheduled 12.5 µm.

discretisation.value: Structured mesh of 12 × 24 cells (576 triangles, 7100 DOF). Finite-strain Reissner–Mindlin shell with quadratic displacements and rotations, linear phase fields, a 9-point surface quadrature rule and a 5-point through-thickness rule. Plane stress is enforced by a local Newton iteration on E33.

reference.quote: A single-edge-notched tension specimen, 12 × 24 structured cells

qois.definition: Fracture energy of the seeded notch. It dominates the assembled energy.
